author: Nadeem Badshah
description:
Allegations of sexual misconduct and predatory behaviour made against ex-comedian who was jailed on Monday

Russell Brand has been accused of sexual misconduct and predatory behaviour by a further six women, according to a report.

The comedian, 51, is accused of having sex with a woman without her consent and then apologising afterwards, an investigation by the Times and the Sunday Times said.

Continue reading...
title: Russell Brand accused of misconduct by six more women, according to report

author: Caitlin Cassidy in Sydney
description:
• Cummins insists he did not know of ball tampering plot in South Africa

  • ‘No masterplan around using illegal methods,’ Cummins says

Pat Cummins has flatly denied Usman Khawaja’s claims that the entire team was implicated in the 2018 sandpaper scandal as “complete and utter nonsense” and “100% wrong” in a defiant appearance at a press conference a week after the allegations came to light.

Appearing before dozens of reporters and cameras at Cricket NSW’s headquarters in Sydney, Cummins refuted the allegations aired in his former teammate’s book, Sabr, and said he had no knowledge of the ball tampering plot in South Africa.

Continue reading...
title: Australia Test captain Pat Cummins calls Khawaja's sandpapergate claims ‘complete and utter nonsense’

author: Kate Lamb
description:
Gibran Rakabuming Raka, the son of former president Joko Widodo, has faced months of questions about his eligibility for office

It has been a turbulent few weeks in Indonesia, with claims the president’s phone was tapped, an uneasy political alliance seemingly in tatters, and now the vice-president resigning after a court ruled he never finished high school.

On the face of it, the drama centres on the educational achievements of vice-president Gibran Rakabuming Raka, but there is more to it than that.

Continue reading...
title: Did Indonesia’s vice-president just resign because he didn’t have a high school diploma?

author: Words by Tereasa Trevor and photographs by Liz Ham
description:
My Uncle Teddy was born 90 years ago into a long line of whip-cracking sideshow folk – his grandmother used to dangle people in the air by her teeth. From contortionists and knife-throwers to a double-jointed horse, he recalls the magic of the showgrounds’ heyday

My uncle Teddy Trevor remembers Casey Nelson, a fellow showman, spruiking his double-jointed horse to sideshow punters in the 1960s. The horse, Nelson warned, was “showing here for the last time”. “Too late, too late will be the cry, when Happy Harry has passed you by,” he called. The act continued for another two decades.

The Casey Nelson tent show, featuring Happy Harry the double-jointed horse, circa the late 1940s

Continue reading...
title: ‘Hurry, hurry, get your tickets now!’: the last of the great Australian showmen – photo essay

author: Nick Visser
description:
Cummins speaks about allegations in Khawaja’s book about the 2018 ball-tampering incident

‘There was no master plan around using illegal methods’

There was no master plan around using illegal methods. I think that’s maybe something that hasn’t been spoken about enough. People assume you have gone from very legal methods to suddenly taking sandpaper and then there must have been some huge master plan.

That is not the case. …

At that stage, you know, even the umpires had a look. We didn’t know it had been altered with sandpaper.

Balls get roughened up every time we play. So, you know, whether that’s from a foreign object or something that’s totally legal and part of the game. Sometimes it’s hard to know. But out there in the field I did not see anything on the ball.
title: Pat Cummins press conference live updates: Australian cricket captain speaks about Usman Khawaja’s ‘sandpapergate’ claims

author: Fiona Harvey in Antalya
description:
Decision disappoints experts hoping for world’s biggest emitter to take global lead on climate crisis

China has ruled out hosting the Cop33 UN climate summit in 2028 after months of deliberations, leaving the field open for other Asian countries to hold it, the Guardian understands.

The decision will disappoint many countries and climate experts, who had hoped the world’s biggest emitter would take the lead on the global stage, as the US under Donald Trump has vacated all forms of international cooperation on the climate.

Continue reading...
title: China rules out hosting Cop33 climate summit in 2028

author: David Hytner at Wembley
description:
It was an historic occasion for Harry Kane, the one when he made his 126th England appearance and overtook Peter Shilton as the nation’s most capped men’s player. And for much of the night, it felt as though the desire to celebrate him, certainly beforehand, was the main thing. The actual football in this Nations League tie felt like a sideshow.

England had demolished Croatia 7-0 in Rijeka last month; it was Croatia’s heaviest ever defeat. It was a different story here. England lacked cut and thrust. There was a flatness to the Wembley atmosphere. Croatia were never likely to be humbled again and they sensed redemption when Petar Sucic capitalised upon a defensive aberration from Jarell Quansah to equalise for 1-1 just before the hour.

Continue reading...
title: Harry Kane spot on to seal England win over Croatia on his record-breaking night

author: Emma Elsworthy and Josh Taylor
description:
An alert on Microsoft’s site said it was ‘aggressively pursuing all pathways to reduce impact’ and blamed a server issue

Microsoft says its servers are beginning to return to service after a global outage resulted in nearly 130,000 users globally reporting issues accessing its 365 suite of software, including Outlook and Teams.

Outage website Down Detector showed a spike in Microsoft 365 problems, with nearly 130,000 reports of issues affecting access to Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook and Teams as well as enterprise services such as SharePoint and OneDrive. AI assistant Copilot was also affected.

Continue reading...
title: Global Microsoft outage affecting Outlook and Teams users, with company ‘restarting’ servers

author: Richard Luscombe
description:
Sightings of the species are becoming increasingly common as experts worry about danger posed by busy waterways

A humpback whale was spotted on Thursday swimming in New York’s Hudson River, sparking a social media frenzy.

Brad Hoylman-Sigal, president of Manhattan borough, was among those to share a photograph of the whale on Facebook, an image taken on Thursday morning and provided by Gotham Whale, a citizen science and education group that tracks marine mammals in New York’s waterways.

Continue reading...
title: Be sea-ing you: humpback whale spotted in New York’s Hudson River

author: Facundo Iglesia in Buenos Aires and Angela Giuffrida in Rome
description:
Leonardo Bertulazzi, ex-member of Italy’s radical far-left Red Brigades, fled in dramatic fashion, ‘like something out of a movie’

As dozens of police and sniffer dogs poured into San Telmo, a traditional Buenos Aires neighbourhood with cobblestone streets, on Tuesday morning, one of the clerks at a shop selling dulce de leche asked them why. He said they were “looking for a bomb”.

It was only later that she found out there was no danger of being blown up after all, and that authorities were, in fact, hunting for a fugitive. “An Italian mafioso, right?” she asked.

Continue reading...
title: Pork fat, a heating pad and a five-storey jump: how a 74-year-old escaped house arrest in Argentina

author: Associated Press
description:
• Death announced by wife, ESPN’s Hannah Storm

  • Hicks had a 35-year career in broadcasting

Sportscaster Dan Hicks, who was the voice of golf, Olympic swimming and Notre Dame football during a 35-year career at NBC Sports, has died, his family and NBC announced Thursday. He was 64.

Hicks died late Wednesday in Connecticut. He died of an acute illness, according to his wife, ESPN broadcaster Hannah Storm.

Continue reading...
title: Dan Hicks, NBC’s voice of golf and Olympic swimming, dies at age of 64 after acute illness

author: Peter Walker Senior political correspondent
description:
Government considers further curbs on non-disclosure agreements after Guardian investigation of TV personality

Ministers are looking at ways to change the law quickly to expand protections that stop non-disclosure agreements being used to cover up harassment or discrimination in the wake of the allegations about David Walliams.

This could involve extending measures that mean an NDA cannot be used this way to silence an employee so that it also applies to others, such as freelancers or volunteers.

Continue reading...
title: UK ministers look at quick ways to limit NDAs after Walliams allegations

author: Guardian sport
description:
• Kane gets England men’s record cap against Croatia

  • Striker starts Nations League game on record 91 goals

Harry Kane has broken the England men’s appearance record after being selected to start the Nations League match against Croatia at Wembley. The striker drew level with Peter Shilton last month and has gone clear with 126 caps.

Kane, who made his debut in March 2015, took his international goals tally to 91 by scoring six times in four games in late September and early October. England’s next-highest scorer, Wayne Rooney, is a distant second with 53 goals.

Continue reading...
title: Harry Kane wins record 126th England cap, pulling clear of Peter Shilton

description: Continue reading...
title: Ben Jennings on the abuse of women and girls in the entertainment industry – cartoon

author: Marina Dunbar
description:
‘We love standards. Well done, Specialist’, the defense secretary writes following Veterans Day visit

  • US politics live – latest updates

The defense secretary, Pete Hegseth, on Thursday awarded a Joint Service Commendation Medal to the soldier who called out him and members of his staff after some in the group were heard laughing and talking near the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier during a Veterans Day visit.

“We love soldiers. We love standards. Well done, Specialist,” Hegseth wrote in a social media post. “Carry on Patriots.” The post included a series of photos of Hegseth with the soldier.

Continue reading...
title: Pete Hegseth awards medal to soldier who reprimanded him near Tomb of the Unknown Soldier

author: Ewan Murray
description:
• Tottenham full-back will make 102nd appearance on Friday

  • ‘It’s another reason to honour one of the greatest players’

Andy Robertson insists his matching of Kenny Dalglish’s Scotland cap record by no means brings reputational parity. Four decades after Dalglish, widely regarded as the country’s finest player, ended his international run at 102 games Robertson will hit the same figure with the visit of North Macedonia to Hampden Park on Friday.

The Tottenham full-back is understandably delighted by his own tally – and should surpass Dalglish in Switzerland on Monday – but paid glowing tribute to the man he got to know well during nine years at Liverpool.

Continue reading...
title: Robertson pays tribute to Dalglish as he matches Scotland cap record

author: Agencies and Guardian sport
description:
• F1 driver urges Israel to let aid into Gaza

  • Trip involved tour of facilities with aid workers

Formula One driver Lewis Hamilton said on Wednesday that Israel must allow aid ⁠trucks into Gaza, a day after he visited the Rafah border crossing in Egypt.

Hamilton, a seven-time ⁠world champion, arrived ⁠in ​El Arish on Tuesday, where he was briefed on how aid is prepared and coordinated before it ⁠is sent into Gaza, as he toured the Rafah crossing and the Egyptian Red Crescent’s aid warehouses.

Continue reading...
title: Lewis Hamilton says ‘Israel’s genocide in Gaza is appalling’ after Rafah visit

author: Simon Burnton
description:
⚽️ WCL updates from 5.45pm GMT kick-off
⚽️ Live scoreboard | And email Simon

Renée Slegers has a bit of a chat about the game, and about how injuries are impacting Arsenal’s squad:

We have an incredible squad, we have a lot of depth in the squad. It’s always going to happen that you have absences. Of course we’re missing those players but we always have players who can step up. We need everyone, so the squad is ready for tonight.

It’s a maze around the Camp Nou building site, and finding the media entrance involved a lot of confused stewards and different directions. We’re in though, and what a stadium it’s going to be when the work is done. It’s really hard to know how Arsenal will fare here. They could snatch a cheeky 1-0 win or lose by five, and neither would be that much of a surprise. It’s great to see Frida Maanum in the 10 and Alessi
title: Barcelona v Arsenal: Women’s Champions League – live

author: Lucy Beaumont
description:
So many have contacted me about their experiences. Women used to be blamed for what men did to them, but I can feel things changing

  • Lucy Beaumont is a comedian and author

At the forefront of everything going on recently are young women and girls. They were vulnerable because of their age or their class, and also because of power dynamics.

These women and girls went through something traumatising, all of them. As did all of the women and girls who I’m sure are coming forward now. Everyone knows there are other men who traumatised girls they’ve worked with, while being paid very, very large amounts of money.

Lucy Beaumont is a comedian and author

Continue reading...
title: Women came forward to protect others. They’re heroes | Lucy Beaumont

author: Kira Lerner
description:
And a politics editor, freshly returned to work after parental leave, can relate

  • This was originally published in the Stakes 2026, a newsletter about the midterm elections. Sign up to get it in your inbox

Most of us probably remember that feeling we had as kids when we would sharpen our pencils and stack fresh notebooks into our backpacks, pick out our favorite outfits, and head back to school in the fall with the energy and exuberance that can only come after a few months away from a classroom.

This Monday, I had the rare adult version of that sensation when I packed my bag for my first day of work after parental leave. And, coincidentally, more than 100 new members of Congress also experienced the first-day jitters as they descended on Washington for new member orientation. For Democrats, who exceeded everyone’s expectat
title: New Democratic lawmakers bring first-day-of-school energy to Capitol Hill

author: Oliver Milman in Antalya
description:
Swedish activist criticised world governments for their failure to prevent environmental breakdown

The planet is “not dying, it is being killed and we know by who”, said Greta Thunberg, who excoriated world governments for their failure to prevent environmental breakdown in her first appearance at the annual UN climate talks in five years.

Thunberg, 23, the Swedish activist who became famous for heading the school climate strike movement, delivered her stark message to those gathered at the Cop31 summit in Antalya, Turkey, amid the ongoing failure by countries to adequately address the climate crisis.

Continue reading...
title: The planet ‘is being killed’, Greta Thunberg tells Cop31 climate summit

author: Jasper Jolly
description:
‘Rules of origin’ on vehicle batteries due to come into force on 1 January if deal on new delay is not reached

  • Business live – latest updates

The UK car industry is preparing to push for a two-year delay to Brexit tariffs on electric cars traded with the EU, after an initial European proposal suggested a shorter delay.

Tariffs are due to kick in on 1 January for the majority of electric cars traded between the EU and UK unless the two sides can come to an agreement to delay for a second time the implementation of “rules of origin” on batteries.

Continue reading...
title: UK car industry to press EU for two-year delay to Brexit EV tariffs

author: Patrick Barkham
description:
To Hold a Mountain tells the incredible story of a woman whose way of life was threatened when she heard her pastures were set to become a Nato training zone

The star of To Hold a Mountain is having trouble with her goats, which keep escaping. So my interview with Mileva “Gara” Jovanović is rescheduled to a moment where the animals are under control and Gara can descend from the peaks to her small winter residence in a small village near the capital of Podorica, for a video call.

“You have to take care of them because they are always searching for their paths,” says Gara, whose Montenegrin is translated into English by Biljana Tutorov, the joint writer-director of the stunning film about Gara’s life in the mountains of Sinjajevina. “But the goats are good, especially when they know the shepherdess. I’m a good shepherdess. They listen to me.”

Continue reading...
title: ‘Goats are good. They listen’: the herder who defeated Montenegro’s military – and can identify her cows’ herby burps

author: Richard Luscombe in Miami
description:
Ron DeSantis signed law prompting the city of Delray Beach to announce it was scrapping its popular Irish celebration

A Florida mayor is working to salvage his city’s St Patrick’s Day parade after it was canceled to comply with a new Republican law banning municipalities from hosting events deemed to promote diversity, equity and inclusion (DEI).

The state’s hard right governor Ron DeSantis signed the law in April that takes effect on 1 January, prompting the city of Delray Beach, near Fort Lauderdale, to announce it was scrapping next year’s popular Irish celebration that regularly attracts tens of thousands of visitors, and also its Pride event.

Continue
title: Florida St Patrick’s Day parade cancelled over Republican anti-DEI law, causing outrage

author: Graham Readfearn in Antalya
description:
Flanked by Greta Thunberg, Rikki Dank says the Australian PM must heed the calls for action on climate change

An indigenous climate activist who is taking the Australian government to the UN human rights committee over its coal and gas exports stood alongside Greta Thunberg at Cop summit to demand Anthony Albanese “stop speaking and start listening.”

Draped in traditional dress in front of a media throng, Rikki Dank, a Gudanji and Wakaya traditional owner, delivered an impassioned plea to Albanese to listen to “the Australian people when they say no more new coal, oil and gas”.

Continue reading...
title: ‘Start listening’: Indigenous activist implores Albanese to block new coal, oil and gas

description:
The Guardian’s picture editors select photographs from around the world

title: Greta Thunberg and a collapsed building in Brooklyn: photos of the day – Thursday

author: Michelle R Smith
description:
Exclusive: Ron Wyden, citing Guardian report, is launching inquiry into whether health secretary lied about Samoa trip during confirmation hearings

A top Democratic senator has launched an investigation into evidence that Robert F Kennedy Jr “unlawfully lied” in his 2025 confirmation hearings to become the US health secretary, citing a report by the Guardian.

Ron Wyden of Oregon, the incoming chair of the powerful Senate finance committee, is seeking extensive records from Children’s Health Defense (CHD), the non-profit anti-vaccine group Kennedy has used as a vehicle to fuel his political rise, including all documents related to a 2019 trip Kennedy took to Samoa.

Continue reading...</
title: Senator opens investigation into evidence RFK Jr ‘unlawfully lied’ to Congress

author: Anna Betts
description:
Local council member says police are looking for suspect, while reports say shooting occurred at or outside of a gym

Multiple people have been shot in north-west Washington DC on Thursday morning, local police confirmed have confirmed, prompting a “barricade situation” in the area.

A spokesperson for the Washington DC police department told the Guardian in a brief phone call on Thursday morning that the scene was “still active”. No further details were immediately available.

Continue reading...
title: Multiple people shot in Washington DC as police warn people to stay inside

author: As told to Dave Simpson
description:
As she continues her farewell tour, the US singer-songwriter answers your questions on romance with Stephen Stills, friendship with Carly Simon and how folk underpins all pop

How did you come into Joni Mitchell’s orbit and how did you end up recording Both Sides, Now before she did? Steve-bayley
I’m 48 years sober, but in the old days I drank. One night in 1967, I was passed out and the phone rang at about 3am. It was my friend [the musician, songwriter and producer] Al Kooper. He said he’d been at a club and had run into this woman, Joni, who wrote songs. He put her on the phone and she sang Both Sides, Now over the phone. It was brilliant. I said: “I’ll be right over.” I recorded it the next day and it became a huge hit.

I don’t think Joni was too happy that I was the first to record it, but she was very generous and I’ve since recorded many of her songs. She was unknow
title: ‘Joni Mitchell sang Both Sides, Now over the phone to me’: folk music legend Judy Collins on her 87 remarkable years

author: Rowena Mason Whitehall editor
description:
Reform leader this week criticised the Labour party for ‘cosying up to’ and ‘promoting’ disgraced comedian

  • UK politics live – latest updates

Nigel Farage appeared on Russell Brand’s US podcast nine months after the comedian was investigated by police over allegations of sexual assault, the Guardian has learned.

The Reform UK leader has criticised Labour for “cosying up to” and “promoting” Brand a decade ago, after the comedian was sentenced this week to more than 10 years in prison for rape and sexual assault.

Continue reading...
title: Farage was guest on Brand podcast after sexual assault investigation began

description:
Film features testimony from 24 Israeli officials involved in surveillance and remote killing of Palestinian civilians

title: NAZA: how and where to watch the Guardian’s acclaimed Gaza documentary

author: Chris Wiegand
description:
Adam Buxton and Joe Cornish returned for a night on stage as packed with pop-culture pisstakes as the show that made them a 90s TV cult. Here’s what we learned

‘Warning: The Adam and Joe Show is a high-density programme.” In the late 90s, that was your Friday-night cue to press record on the video player for Adam Buxton and Joe Cornish’s pop-culture potpourri of sketches, pranks and lovingly crafted, lo-fi movie parodies featuring figurines and cuddly toys. Thirty years after its debut, the duo – now both 57 – recreated their old den in the improbable environs of the Royal Albert Hall for a three-hour anniversary show as packed as the rapid-fire series. Here’s a select few things we learned from an evening of clips, chat and ridiculously catchy songs …

Continue reading...
title: Adam and Joe on spoofing ‘Christopher No-Laughs’ with a toys’ Odyssey – and Patrick Stewart’s haunted house

author: Rajeev Syal Home affairs editor
description:
Mostafa Sepahvand and Farhad Javadi Manesh carried out surveillance in an effort to inflict violence on targets

Two men of Iranian origin who were hired through social media as part of a plan to “eliminate” journalists in the UK have been found guilty of engaging in conduct likely to assist Tehran’s intelligence services.

Mostafa Sepahvand, 41, and Farhad Javadi Manesh, 46, carried out surveillance and reconnaissance between August 2024 and March last year in an attempt to inflict violence on “subjects” in the UK.

Continue reading...
title: Two men found guilty over Iranian attempts to ‘eliminate’ UK-based journalists

author: Clive Paget
description:
Orliński/Devieilhe/Il Pomo d’Oro/Corti
(Erato)
Francesco Corti keeps the drama on the boil in this period instrument recording of Handel’s opera, with herculean feats of vocal dexterity by Jakub Józef Orliński in the title role – but it’s Sabine Devieilhe’s breathtaking queen who steals the show

Giulio Cesare is Handel’s most popular opera with at least 15 versions in the current catalogue, several of them historical. This new recording by period instrument band Il Pomo d’Oro comes off the back of a European tour, thus benefiting from the experience of live performances. A lived-in quality is palpable here, from the frisson of emotional risk-taking to imaginatively decorated da capo sections.

Leading from the keyboard, Francesco Corti keeps the drama on the boil, especially in recitatives where his resonant harpsichord sits comfortably in the mix. Timings are similar to
title: Giulio Cesare in Egitto album review – Sabine Devieilhe’s exquisite Cleopatra could make stones weep

author: Eleanor Gordon-Smith
description:
Children vary just like the rest of us, writes advice columnist Eleanor Gordon-Smith. You don’t know you’re bad with this baby yet, because you don’t know them yet

  • Read more Leading questions

My best friend is having her first child. I am so happy for her and I know she’s going to be a stellar parent. However, I am not good with babies and have issues I need to work on from being told and not asked to babysit a lot as a teenager. I don’t know how to respond without coming off as a total jerk if she ever asks me and my fiance to babysit.

What can I do to still be a supportive friend and how do I clear the air on the matter?

Continue reading...
title: My best friend is pregnant. I’m happy for her but not good with babies. How can I be supportive? | Leading questions

author: Xiaoying You
description:
Battery maker CATL aims to have 2,000 swapping stations in China by the end of 2027 and to bring the tech to Europe

Every day, Wang Bing drives his big electric lorry to send about five tonnes of goods between the cities of Haikou and Dongfang on Hainan, a tropical island in southern China. A round trip covers about 500 kilometres (310 miles). But refuelling is not something Wang worries about.

“When my battery runs low, I just drive my truck into a battery-swapping station to get a fully charged one,” says the 53-year-old, who shares the journey with a colleague in eight-hour shifts.

Continue reading...
title: ‘It is much, much faster’: could China’s battery-swapping e-trucks be the answer to EV range anxiety?

author: Ed Aarons
description:
A losing run, set-piece struggles and a call for help led Steve Parish to cut ties with the manager after five months

The moment that summed up Crystal Palace’s season under Pierre Sage came five minutes before half-time at Selhurst Park on Sunday. After Palace had gone close to taking the lead on numerous occasions against Liverpool, the Frenchman must have feared the worst when Alexis Mac Allister headed in from a soft free-kick conceded by Jefferson Lerma. The TV cameras immediately panned to Steve Parish in the stands. After the Palace chair removed his hands from in front of his eyes, his expression said everything you needed to know. The only surprise was that Sage had to wait until Thursday before his inevitable fate was confirmed.

N
title: Pierre Sage’s failure to fix defensive flaws leaves Crystal Palace seeking new solution

author: Associated Press
description:
Authorities say the boy was in the care of Michael Comer’s mother, but she left him with her son to run an errand

An 11-month-old South Carolina boy who authorities say was buried alive in a dog crate by his father was found by rescuers after about 24 hours, crying and covered in dirt, his grandfather said about the dramatic rescue.

But soon after, little Koah Sharp stopped crying, John Comer told the Associated Press on Wednesday night as he recalled the events that played out the day before in the woods on his neighbor’s property. The infant was put on the back of a truck and sat up, Comer said.

Continue reading...
title: Father of South Carolina infant who survived being buried alive charged with attempted murder

author: Mujtaba Rahman
description:
European leaders need urgently to prepare for a far-right French president who would cut off Kyiv’s financial lifeline

Europe is consumed by two debates that matter less than it thinks, while neglecting one that matters enormously. The first is who should represent the EU in negotiations with Russia. This is largely irrelevant because there is little prospect of serious Ukraine peace talks before the end of winter - despite the fanfare that has surrounded discussions in Abu Dhabi this week. Russia has powerful incentives to escalate the war over the coming months in an attempt to break Ukraine’s economy and civilian morale.

The second is Donald Trump’s approach to Ukraine. This matters less than it once did – and not only because he is now more constrained by a Democratic Congress. Since returning to office in January 2025, Trump has provided
title: Trump won't save Ukraine. But Marine Le Pen's betrayal could be worse | Mujtaba Rahman

author: Rachel Savage in Johannesburg and agencies
description:
After a month-long investigation it was concluded that Kundizeza’s story The Blue Fighter, which won the £10,000 Caine prize, was ‘human-written’

Zimbabwean author Simbarashe Kundizeza has been cleared of using AI to write a prize-winning short story, after the prestigious Caine prize for African writers concluded that his entry was “human-written” after a month-long investigation.

Kundizeza’s story The Blue Fighter, which charts the declining fortunes of a family after the father invests in fish tanks, was announced as the winner of the £10,000 prize on 6 October.

Continue reading...
title: Zimbabwean author Simbarashe Kundizeza cleared of using AI to write prize-winning story

author: Richard Luscombe and agency
description:
Mayor Zohran Mamdani says crews are working through ‘extremely dangerous conditions’ to find anyone trapped

Rescue crews continued to search for survivors in the rubble of a collapsed building in Brooklyn, New York, at first light on Thursday as the death toll rose to eight.

Authorities in New York City said at least 17 people were hurt when the three-story residential building on the edge of a construction site in the borough’s Flatbush section collapsed at about 4pm on Wednesday.

Continue reading...
title: Brooklyn building collapse kills at least 8 and injures 17 as search continues

author: Richard Partington Senior economics correspondent
description:
Despite John Healey’s defiance, the economy faces threats from a tech slowdown and energy bills this winter

  • AI helps UK economy grow at fastest pace for more than two years

The forecasters were clear when John Healey became chancellor in July: Britain’s resilience to the war in the Middle East would not last. The global economic headwinds were too strong, inflation was beginning to rise and growth would slow to a trickle.

Four months into the job, the economy is continuing to defy expectations after growing by 0.7% in the third quarter – the fastest expansion in two and a half years. It puts the UK on course to be the second-fastest growing G7 economy this year.
title: AI helped UK defy expectations – but will economy’s resilience fizzle out?

author: Jessica Rawnsley in San Miguelito, Panama
description:
For decades, mountains of waste have blighted poor neighbourhoods on the edge of the city. But as the problems spread, a belated reckoning is under way

Life in San Miguelito has long been dictated by rubbish. Routes to the shop are carefully navigated to avoid pungent mountains of rotting waste, some visible from space. Driving during the rainy season is a perilous obstacle course, dodging black bin bags and rusty fridges in the middle of the road. Children are taught early to avoid the river, the rubbish, the rats, yet mosquito-borne diseases still stalk the community.

For Yamileth, who lives with her family on one of the steep, narrow streets that thread the hillside neighbourhood, the waste is a constant backdrop to daily life. Mornings are punctuated by the stench and buzz of flies, and in the evenings you can hear rats scuttling and stray dogs rustling as they rip open bags in search of food among the rubbish heaps, known in slang as patacones (also the na
title: Rats, dengue and an all-day stench: can Panama City solve its waste crisis?

author: Moira Donegan
description:
At a time when individual men wield massive power, the ramifications of the Nvidia CEO’s affair could be enormous

One of the reasons you want to distribute power and responsibility in powerful organizations and high-stakes enterprises is so that the narcissism or myopia of one man do not come to carry outsized consequences.

When power is spread out across multiple people, it matters less if one of those people is prone to flattery, or in the midst of a midlife crisis, or perhaps just a bit stupid; the limits on his power become limits on the fallout of his character flaws.

Continue reading...
title: Thanks to American oligarchy, Jensen Huang’s midlife crisis is a problem for all of us | Moira Donegan

author: Presented by Madeleine Finlay with Ian Sample , produced by Joshan Chana, Luke John Smith and Jacob Liebenberg , the executive producer was Ellie Bury
description:
An alternative to BMI for diagnosing obesity could prevent misdiagnosis in millions of people worldwide, according to doctors who found it more accurately distinguished healthy people from those with harmful excess body fat. Guardian Science editor Ian Sample takes co-host Madeleine Finlay through why BMI is flawed, and how the new framework could improve precision medicine.

Continue reading...
title: Obesity: how to stop millions being misdiagnosed - video

author: Guardian sport and agencies
description:
• Kerr admits concern is ‘high’ for Curry’s injury

  • Bassey says Smart guilty of ‘fake toughness’

Kevin Durant scored 20 points, Alperen Sengun and Amen Thompson added 19 and the Houston Rockets snapped Golden State’s eight-game winning streak with a 115-108 victory on Wednesday night.

The Warriors played most of the game without Stephen Curry after the star left in the first quarter with right abdominal soreness and didn’t return. He was due to get an MRI on the injury.

Continue reading...
title: Smart ejected for punching Bassey as Warriors lose Curry to injury in defeat to Rockets

author: Seham Tantesh in Gaza and William Christou in Beirut
description:
Hospital director says 28 wounded in attack on one of few remaining medical facilities in the strip

An Israeli airstrike on Nasser hospital in southern Gaza killed six people, including a surgeon and a disabled man, and wounded 28 others, according to the hospital director.

The Israeli military carried out the attack on the hospital, in Khan Younis, early on Thursday saying in a statement it had struck a Hamas commander and other fighters there, without providing evidence.

Continue reading...
title: Israeli airstrike on Nasser hospital in Gaza kills surgeon and five others

author: Alexis Petridis
description:
(XL Recordings)
His Playboi Carti collabs may have dragged Tom Heyes out of the underground, but this bracing debut remains far from the mainstream, full of garbled barks and walls of noise

On the second track on his debut album, Tom Heyes accuses lesser artists of copying him. “What the fuck you even take me for?” he barks on Northside Needs Me, over a grinding, distorted bassline that comes punctuated with stammering, rave-y vocal samples. “Too much noise shit, replicating what I played before.”

Of course, charging that others are merely imitating what you did previously is a venerable rap tradition: the track that gave said practice its longstanding name, Bite’n My Stylee by Original Concept, is now 40 years old. Perhaps it’s true that others have been copying the approach that Heyes has minted under the alias of Blackhaine, but if so, it seems faintly remarkable, because his approach is so determinedly u
title: Blackhaine: Saints in the Wethouse review | Alexis Petridis's album of the week

author: Isha Remal, as told to Jonathan Watts
description:
She was sleeping in when the house started shaking. Then her mum called. This is Isha Remal’s story

Location: Bidur, Nepal

Disaster: Floods, 2026

Isha Remal is a 17-year-old volunteer for the Red Cross Society in Bidur, Nepal. This summer, her family was caught up in the floods that crashed through the country after a glacier collapsed – an event made more likely by climate change

Continue reading...
title: ‘I was home alone when the glacier collapsed. My mum called and told me to run’ – This is climate breakdown

author: Jamie Jackson
description:
Disastrous decisions and confused appointments have been a constant theme at Old Trafford since Sir Alex Ferguson’s retirement in 2013

For a window into the alarming dysfunction at Manchester United that Michael Carrick failed to manage and caused his sacking, consider the case of Eddie Howe, initially a favourite to succeed the 45-year-old before Mauricio Pochettino’s emergence as the chosen one.

The former Newcastle manager had been Jason Wilcox’s choice to take over from Carrick. Howe was also the favoured candidate of Dan Ashworth, Wilcox’s predecessor as United’s director of football, to follow Erik ten Hag after the Dutchman’s sacking in October 2024. Except Wilcox disagreed and Sir Jim Ratcliffe went with Wilcox’s man, Ruben Amorim, and that December Ashworth departed only five months after joining.
title: Michael Carrick was just the latest fall guy for Manchester United’s dysfunctional hierarchy | Jamie Jackson

author: Alice Speri
description:
Members of Democratic Socialists of America have a unique opportunity to fulfill campaign promises and group’s ideals

As progressive candidates scored wins across the country last week, a historic number of socialists swept into power – in Congress, in state legislatures and at the helm of American cities.

Democratic Socialists of America members Nithya Raman and Janeese Lewis George were elected to lead the second largest US city – Los Angeles – and the capital – Washington DC respectively. Two other young DSA members, David Morales and Yousef Rabhi, were elected mayors of Providence, Rhode Island, and Ann Arbor, Michigan. They will join a handful of socialist mayors in sm
title: A record number of US democratic socialists will become mayors. They’re out to prove their vision for affordability

author: Charlie Brinkhurst-Cuff
description:
Claire Emslie and Emma Kelly are among those taking advantage of new research and guidelines for pregnant players

Claire Emslie wasn’t expecting to be able to run at 81% of her max speed at 32 weeks pregnant.

Emslie, a Scotland international who also plays as a forward for Angel City FC, documented her journey through pregnancy and football training on social media and is part of a growing number of professional female footballers who are getting pregnant in their athletic prime and approaching motherhood with a fresh mindset. Rather than marking the end of a career (notably, Millie Bright announced her pregnancy in September, months after having retired), pregnancy can mark both a continuation and a renewal.
title: ‘Pregnancy does not mean game over’: meet the footballers challenging the myths | Moving the Goalposts

author: Owen Jones
description:
It’s naive to think the Israeli opposition will act very differently. Look at what it has said about even the most vulnerable Palestinians

“Every child, every baby in Gaza is the enemy.” In a normal society, a politician who said something so depraved would face total reputational ruin. Not so in Israel. Meet Moshe Feiglin, previously considered a “far-right outcast”, who has just been elected to Israel’s legislature. He said this last May, but he has also called for more Palestinian babies to die and for Gaza’s entire population, newborns included, to be expelled. In last month’s
title: Time for a harsh truth: even with Netanyahu gone, the killing won’t stop in Gaza | Owen Jones

author: Luke McLaughlin
description:
⚽️ Head coach departs after one win in 11 games
⚽️ Carrick sacked with Pochettino poised to take over
⚽️ Have any thoughts? Email Luke

“After going through the Moyes season,” writes Hugh, “the dross football of Mourinho and Van Gaal, the moments-years of Solskjaer, the Rangnick surgery that never was, the middling Ten Hag, the baffling Amorim, and now a decent man thrust into the meat grinder, this is the first year it’s been genuinely hard to watch Man Utd with any emotion.

“And it’s not because of the football. It’s that the Glazer ownership and Ratcliffe mismanagement has met the Man City revelations, meaning it’s hard to see the point anymore. £1bn taken out of the club while others were illicitly pumping in roughly the same. A club drained of life, hollowed out … I can
title: Carrick sacked by Manchester United with team in Premier League relegation zone – live

author: Aditya Chakrabortty
description:
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s affair must be the costliest fling in human history – and a preview of what awaits when the tech bubble bursts

One thing we all know about the tech billionaires is they are super-smart. We know this largely because they never stop telling us. The “cognitive elite”, to use their favoured phrase, are entitled to shape our future without our say-so. When Elon Musk goes hiring, he wants “super-high-IQ small-government revolutionaries”. Long before they got private jets, what fuelled these boys was faith in their own brainpower. As a teenager, Jensen Huang wooed his future wife, Lori, thus: “If you do homework with me every Sunday, I promise you you’ll get straight As.”

Lord Byron: I believe it’s your move.
title: Billions lost and markets roiled by one man’s indiscretion. Isn’t it now clear that these tech bros are too powerful? | Aditya Chakrabortty

author: Nicola Davis Science correspondent
description:
Unprecedented view of cosmos provided by Euclid mission throws up many more cases of gravitational lensing

A mission to create the largest ever 3D map of the universe has revealed more than 900m galaxies in its first major data release together with about 15,000 potential cases of a phenomenon that could help unlock the secrets of the “dark universe”.

Launched in July 2023, the European Space Agency’s Euclid mission promised to create the largest cosmic map ever made, encompassing a third of the sky and more than 10bn years of cosmic history.

Continue reading...
title: European survey reveals 900m galaxies – and possibly secrets of ‘dark universe’

author: Sarah Butler
description:
CEO says ‘democratic approach’ has helped brand outperform tough market, with big rises in China and US

Burberry has returned to profit as its back to basics strategy drove strong sales of the British brand’s coats, jackets and handbags over the summer.

Joshua Schulman, the chief executive, said the luxury brand had outperformed a “challenging luxury market” to achieve sales growth of 6%, helped by strong online and wholesale sales particularly in China and the US. “Our strategy is working,” he said.

Continue reading...
title: Burberry returns to profit as sales soar, from £85 socks to £9,000 bags

author: Luke McLaughlin
description:
Midfielder’s old-school attributes came to the fore during Nottingham Forest’s win against Manchester City

Modern football is more systematised and data-driven than ever but some things never change. Winning the first ball is important but the second ball – the Holy Grail for Sunday league footballers – is often more so.

Nottingham Forest’s 3-1 win against Manchester City last weekend featured a classic example. Forest led 2-1 inside the last 20 minutes but City, lifted by Rayan Cherki’s sweet half-volley, were pushing for an equaliser.

Continue reading...
title: ‘Second ball’ may be a Sunday league mantra but Yates showed its top-flight relevance

author: Benjamin Lee
description:
The It Follows and Longlegs star tears into the role of a murderous governess in this hit-and-miss adaptation of Virginia Feito’s gory novel

It’s not that hard to figure out why a lower-class woman toiling away in Victorian England would be so easily driven to violently murder everyone around her. If it’s not the brittle entitlement of those who employ you, it’s the unending misogyny of the system you’re forced to be a subservient part of, all the while being underpaid and undervalued and at the mercy of sexual violence, a multitude of diseases and an average lifespan of just 42.

As Winifred Notty (Maika Monroe) fills the frame in Victorian Psycho, heading to a new job as governess for a rich family, it’s easy to be on her side. Even as her murderous impulses start to rear their head, they’re made somewhat understandable, although Winifred isn’t just a woman reacting to the various injustices of the time – she’s one responding to a demon within her, a darkness she has c
title: Victorian Psycho review – Maika Monroe has a blast in unsteady horror romp

author: Alexandra Talty
description:
Proponents argue ocean carbon removal is necessary to counteract the effects of the climate crisis but critics say more research is needed

A cluster of candy cane-striped smoke stacks dots the horizon of Tufts Cove in Nova Scotia, Canada. Deep in the briny depths of Halifax harbour, something huge is happening: the ocean is being engineered to remove atmospheric carbon.

“This is what Mother Nature has done naturally for a few billion years in order to rebalance the atmospheric and ocean chemistry over long timescales,” says Dr Greg Rau, co-founder and senior scientist at Planetary Technologies.

Continue reading...
title: First guidelines on attempts to manipulate the ocean put spotlight on geoengineering industry

author: Steve Rose
description:
It is built of wood, resembles an Ikea and its power is totally renewable. Plus, it was built with the local community in mind. Is this facility in Falun the best datacentre in the world?

‘It was pretty cool, when they were building it. It looked like a very large Ikea,” says John Wernvik, of EcoDataCenter. He is giving me a tour of their facility in Falun, Sweden, which could lay claim to being the world’s greenest datacentre – although to many, that is a contradiction in terms.

One difference is immediately visible: this datacentre is made out of wood. Huge panels of cross-laminated timber arrived at the site pre-cut, and were assembled by crane according to instructions, like flatpack furniture. Aesthetically, this section of the datacentre is more like an Ikea before the fit-out, a cavernous, echoey, immaculately clean hangar. The wood is not EcoDataCenter’s only claim to sustainability; it is more than just cosmetic, says Wernvik, the company’s chief external relat
title: Datacentres are deeply unpopular. Has Sweden made one we can all love?

author: Sam Wolfson
description:
As public mood has shifted on Israel-Gaza and the Iran war, so has the manosphere’s devotion to the US president

Earlier this week, Donald Trump announced that the UFC president, Dana White, was to become his press secretary. The US president hoped the creator of Power Slap, a face-slapping league which one of the world’s leading neurologists called “a sport inconsistent with the intelligence of humans”, might be the right man to deliver his daily rebuttals to the media.

Trump later backtracked on the appointment, saying he was “only kidding”, yet it is easy to understand why he might be pining for White’s muscles, trash talk and thirst for athletic violence. White is representative of the way Trump transcended politics in 2024 to become a celebrated fig
title: ‘Maga is dead, Maga is effeminate’: why has the manosphere rejected Trump?

author: Hosted by Kai Wright , produced by Anabel Bacon and Tiara Chiaramonte , engineered by Ivan Kuraev , executive producer Jonathan Menjivar
description: Pete Hegseth has managed to dodge an impeachment trial, for the second time. And Republicans have avoided — for now — a major public accounting of the damage done at the Pentagon during Hegseth’s tenure. Thomas Massie’s articles of impeachment detail charges that are likely to return when Democrats take the majority next year. Kai Wright speaks with Guardian senior political enterprise reporter Aram Roston about how people inside the military have reacted to the impeachment and to Hegseth’s tenure, from the boat strikes in the Caribbean to the massive loss of experienced leadership and a dramatic depletion of munitions in Iran. Roston, who has covered the Pentagon across several administrations, describes a Pentagon shaken up in ways he’s never before seen.
title: Pete Hegseth’s wake of destruction at the Pentagon – Stateside with Kai and Carter

author: Mohamad Bazzi
description:
Voters remembered Trump’s many promises to avoid the same kind of regime-change wars started by his predecessors

For much of his political career, Donald Trump ranted at past US presidents who got the US entangled in endless foreign conflicts. He used it as a cudgel to belittle his predecessors, calling George W Bush’s decision to invade Iraq in 2003 “the worst single mistake ever made in the history of our country”. Trump also regularly derided the occupation of Afghanistan as “a total disaster”.

Then Trump decided to launch his own disastrous war against Iran eight months ago. And that conflict may well have cost Republicans control of Congress in last week’s midterm elections.
title: Trump ran on a platform of peace. His war may have cost Republicans the midterms | Mohamad Bazzi

author: Jamie Jackson
description:
• Club pay tribute to ‘legend’ but say change ‘necessary’

  • Pochettino wants Premier League return after USA spell

Manchester United have sacked Michael Carrick as their head coach with the team in the Premier League’s relegation zone and lined up Mauricio Pochettino to take over.

Pochettino has a framework agreement to join a club who have one win from their past 11 matches. The USA head coach, a Premier League manager with Southampton, Tottenham and Chelsea, has a release clause of about $10m (£7.5m). United will have to pay more to take his staff.

Continue reading...
title: Michael Carrick sacked by Manchester United with Pochettino poised to take over

author: Briana Ellis-Gibbs
description:
A Long Shadow: Postwar Japan Through the Lens will be the first show of Japanese photography in more than three decades at New York’s Metropolitan Museum of Art. The exhibit brings together 15 intergenerational artists as well as photographic prints, including more than 25 books and magazines and a video installation, all combining to show how photographers in Japan documented the country in the decades after the second world war. The exhibition runs until 2 May 2027

Continue reading...
title: Punks, sex workers and society in transition: documenting postwar Japan – in pictures

author: Christian Donlan
description:
Nintendo Switch/2, PlayStation 4/5, Xbox One/series X/S, PC; Denkiworks/Inpleron Limited
This gentle game of fixing and fetching, in which you play as a furry post office worker on a BMX, has a slow, calming magic that delights in routine and restoration

Arriving alongside November’s blue wave, Tanuki: Pon’s Summer is a game of quiet restoration that feels perfectly suited to the current moment. Tasked with repairing an ancient shrine in the weeks leading up to a local festival, you’ll find yourself cleaning out trash, mending broken arches and slowly bringing a small rural community back together.

It sounds a bit like JL Carr’s compact but enchanting novel A Month in the Country, except instead of shell-shocked veterans of the first world war you’re left exploring
title: Tanuki: Pon’s Summer review – an adorable raccoon mends the world, one parcel at a time

author: Graham Searles
description:
With the season reaching its halfway point, it’s time to see which teams and players are excelling

Josh Allen, QB, Buffalo Bills. Joe Burrow is excelling for the Bengals and is rightly a frontrunner for MVP. He’s stylish, precise and mentally rock-solid, everything a franchise needs. But is he the most thrilling quarterback in the NFL? Right now, Allen is box office each and every week. But it’s not just the entertainment factor: Allen has a weaker supporting cast than Burrow and many of the other MVP contenders – imagine what he could do with Ja’Marr Chase as a teammate – and yet the Bills top the AFC at 7-1 thanks in large part to his passing and hammering runs.

Continue reading...
title: NFL midseason awards: Allen’s brilliance, a Seahawks shocker and a new Super Bowl pick

author: Daniel Boffey in Hamburg
description:
Exclusive: Legal notice comes as Buenos Aires ramps up rhetoric over UK territory and seeks to halt Sea Lion project

The Argentinian government threatened a British businessman involved in an offshore Falkland Islands oil project with jail, the Guardian can reveal.

Sam Moody, the chief executive of Rockhopper Exploration, and his company’s chief financial officer received the correspondence this autumn as Buenos Aires began ramping up its rhetoric over the British overseas territory.

Continue reading...
title: Argentina threatens UK oil firm CEO with jail over Falklands drilling

author: Ima Caldwell
description:
Island state declares it ‘is not really for tourists’ – but is the marketing strategy just a cheeky piece of reverse psychology?

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Research shows “tourists hate themselves” – which is exactly why the marketing flacks at Tourism Tasmania are telling them to stay away from the island state.

Its new campaign declares the island state is “not really for tourists”, enlisting former SBS newsreader Lee Lin Chin to help sell the tongue-in-cheek campaign, based on the idea that Australians prefer identifying as a “traveller” rather than a “tourist”.

Co
title: ‘Tourists hate themselves’ – which is why Tasmania is telling them to stay away

author: Jonathan Liew
description:
Left out of squad to tour South Africa, spin bowler’s exclusion points to a sport reshaped by the needs of T20 and hard data

During the summer, Sky Sports would frequently run an advert for one of English cricket’s blue-chip financial sponsors. I forget its exact name – something like WXYZ Tradify or Crypto Max 301 or Wealth Centaur would be my guess. But I remember there was a mind-shreddingly banal male voiceover (“diversify your forex contingents and start making your money bleed today”), to which England players like Harry Brook and Jacob Bethell were depicted engaging in various feats of staged cricketing heroism. Right up until the moment Shoaib Bashir steps up to bowl.

Bashir delivers his trademark off-break with that famously high release point. Upon which Bethell steps down the track and smashes the Wealth Centaur-brande
title: Fizzle of Shoaib Bashir’s algorithmic magic echoes wider decline of Test spin | Jonathan Liew

author: Andrew Beasley
description:
Striker to play historic 126th match and that’s far from the only statistic that sets him apart for his country

Harry Kane will become the most capped player for England’s men when he features against Croatia at Wembley. Yet in the context of the grand history of international football, his record total will be relatively low.

Kane will draw level with players including Dani Alves, Eden Hazard and Paolo Maldini on 126 caps. Illustrious players, none of whom lead their country’s appearance standings. Neither do Kevin De Bruyne or Luís Figo, on 127, or Manuel Neuer with 128. It will be some time next year before England’s captain enters European football’s top 50 players for international caps, never mind the global standings.

Continue reading...
title: Harry Kane’s England caps record: an illustrious career in numbers and charts

author: Philippa Kelly
description:
Her witty photos served as a rebuttal to 80s misogyny and Thatcherite conservatism. Now 50 years on, the photographer is receiving an overdue retrospective. ‘I loved that we could respond with humour,’ she says.

If it were a lady it would get its bottom pinched. If this lady was a car she’d run you down.” These are the words that Jill Posener immortalised in November 1979, when she picked her way through traffic on London’s Farringdon Road to photograph something most would have overlooked: a graffitied billboard. The first sentence was there by design – a sexist attempt at wit intended to promote a new Fiat. The second she has since been repeatedly accused of adding herself.

In reality, the image-maker, playwright and nonprofit founder explains from her home in California, the now infamous phrase had been daubed by two women working at the nearby offices of the socialist newspaper Morning Star. “They had seen the billboard go up and were so incensed that they came up w
title: ‘I railed against the stereotype of the humourless lesbian’: the cheeky, feminist photography of Jill Posener

author: John Duerden
description:
Japan FA honorary president is hoping a calmer approach that makes fewer unwelcome headlines for Fifa will be welcomed by football

Not many remember Japan’s bid for the 2022 World Cup, when the country finished the race with only two of the final 22 votes. Kozo Tashima was involved then, and now the honorary president of the Japan Football Association is going it alone in the hope of ousting Gianni Infantino.

The 68-year-old Tashima is an unlikely insurgent and an unlikely challenger to Infantino. He is, however, a familiar and respected figure in Asian and global football politics, and ready to take the Fifa presidency out of the headlines into a quieter era.

Continue reading...
title: Less drama, more listening, but is Kozo Tashima the candidate to topple Infantino?

author: Zoe Williams
description:
It didn’t need a novel: even Leave voters understand the damage that has been done, as does the PM. Now all he has to do is persuade his party

Earlier this week, some people on the radio were talking about a very British dystopia. The government had disintegrated, but everyone was carrying on pretty much as they had before. Britain was isolated on the world stage and people missed Europe like hell, but weren’t allowed to visit, let alone live there.

I thought the radio people were discussing Britain post-Brexit, circa 2022. In fact, they were talking about the plot of the Booker prize-winning novel The End of Everything. Its author, M John Harrison, is renowned now for being, at 81, the oldest winner of the award, as well as the first science fiction writer to win it. But let’s also carve out a space for him on the podium of dystopian fiction, as a wr
title: The Booker prize winner described a dystopian Britain. But haven’t we been living in that since Brexit? | Zoe Williams

author: Interviews by Georgina Lawton
description:
Maddie drives Nadia mad with her disjointed conversations, but doesn’t think she should have to make an appointment to phone her sister. Who’s in the wrong? You make the call

• Find out how to get a disagreement settled or become a juror

Maddie rings at the worst moments. It’s usually when she’s on the train and I can’t even hear her

Continue reading...
title: You be the judge: should my sister stop calling me when she’s on the move?

author: Ajit Niranjan
description:
World leaders including UK prime minister Andy Burnham are addressing the summit today, as talks head into the third day

First up is Taneti Maamau, President of Kiribati, who was scheduled to speak yesterday. He’s calling to phase out fossil fuels and speed up global electrification, underscoring what failure means for our shared humanity. “Every delay puts lives at risk. I urge this summit to act boldly so Cop31 is remembered for moral clarity, unity and decisive action.”

The world is heading for an “irrecoverable overshoot” of global temperature thresholds that will plunge billions of people into disastrous climate impacts because governments have stalled for so long to cut planet-heating emissions, analysis has found.

Continue reading...
title: Cop31: ‘The crisis is upon us now’, Burnham tells climate summit

author: Sandra Newman
description:
The Teenage Sex and Death at Camp Miasma writer-director’s first novel is a wry, hugely fun journey into the dark world behind our screens

Public Access Afterworld is the first novel by Jane Schoenbrun, director of cult-hit horror film I Saw the TV Glow and the more recent Teenage Sex and Death at Camp Miasma; movies in which screens are a permeable barrier and people are menaced by the uncanny realms that lurk behind them. Here the main character is Bethany Peters, a young trans woman working as a content moderator at a YouTube-like company called GlobalVill. Her job is to watch “offensive, illegal, disturbing videos that have no place on the internet” and press a red button to remove those that violate the code of conduct. One night she sees a video posted by someone with the username JulesPublicAccessAfterworld, a visibly malnourished non-binary kid who reminds Bethany of herself “before her stay in hospital, and everything that happened to her there”. The kid sa
title: Public Access Afterworld by Jane Schoenbrun review – horror in the TV static

author: Sarah King
description:
As a child, Jonny Trunk never went on holiday – perhaps that’s why he started collecting vintage brochures that showed glamorous beaches and cruises (but never the malfunctioning toilets)

Continue reading...
title: Wish you were here? Retro holiday guides – in pictures

author: Dara Kerr and agencies
description:
The meeting comes after the executive and co-founder admitted to having a romantic relationship with a woman who is alleged to be a Chinese spy

Nvidia’s board of directors met on Wednesday to decide whether to oust Jensen Huang as CEO of the world’s most valuable chip company, according to multiple reports, after a tumultuous week in which the executive and co-founder of the company admitted to having a romantic relationship with a woman who is alleged to be a Chinese spy.

The meeting marks ⁠a sharp shift from Sunday, when Nvidia’s board ​expressed confidence in Huang and his leadership team, and the company’s stock slid more than 8% in after-hours trading after the Wall Street Journal reported that ⁠the company was preparing to fire Huang.
title: Nvidia board reportedly deciding whether to oust CEO Jensen Huang as stock price plunges

author: Zan Times reporters
description:
The unofficial Taliban restriction has forced women into desperate and absurd situations as they seek medical help, according to interviews given to the Guardian and Zan Times

Farida*, 37, woke up in excruciating pain one night with a toothache. Over the next few days, the pain intensified. “My teeth had been ruined for years. My molars on both sides of my mouth were severely damaged. I couldn’t sleep at night and could barely eat.”

Farida and her family had returned from Iran earlier this year to live in Herat, a city in western Afghanistan. Like many migrants forced to return, they have struggled to find work and income. In their straitened circumstances, visiting a doctor has become a luxury but the pain forced Farida to a dental clinic in the Bakrabad area of Herat in early July.
title: Afghan women told to ‘go home’ after de facto ban on male doctors treating them

author: Exclusive by Sean Ingle
description:
• Creation of Sport Org sparks disquiet at governing bodies

  • Smaller sports concerned they might be taken over

The leaders of Britain’s Olympic and Paralympic sports have been responsible for some of the country’s greatest successes over the past two decades. But there are changes afoot that are increasingly ruffling feathers and stoking fears.

Most people will not have heard of Sport Org, the organisation recently set up by UK Sport. Essentially, it evolved out of British Curling, and now uses its leaders and expertise across curling, para-curling, para table tennis, squash and, from 2030, bobsleigh and skeleton.

Continue reading...
title: ‘All-out war’: UK sports fear an uncertain future after new body created

author: Emine Saner
description:
The British actor took up writing and producing to have control over what she stars in after a scandal involving some of the most powerful men in the film business

After a recent run as an assassin, a serial killer and a gangster, Charlotte Kirk was looking for something a little lighter, and surely nothing can be more jolly, more wholesome than a Christmas romcom. In Christmas & Chaos, Kirk plays Sadie, a pop star in search of a hit – or, to be more precise, three hits for a new musical by an impresario (a comedic Jason Isaacs who only appears on screen via video call). She has just a couple of weeks to come up with something with handsome-and-heartbroken composer (Ben McGregor).

Kirk, who also produced the film, approached Jamie Adams, director of several low-budget British films, including Black Mountain Poets, intrigued by his regular use of improvisation. They worked out the story together, says Kirk, but made it without a script. All they knew was that “this w
title: ‘I trusted a lot of people, and the wrong people, and I shouldn’t have’: Charlotte Kirk on navigating Hollywood

author: Rachel Roddy
description:
This soft-but-dense, velvety delight is cake at its most pudding-like. It’s at its prime still warm from the oven, but gets gloriously fudgy after a night in the fridge

The note by Elizabeth David is helpful here: “This cake can also be eaten like a pudding” for its soft-dense-velvet-texture. But I am jumping ahead: this week’s column started in Ferrara, a city in the wetlands of the Po delta in the north-eastern corner of Emilia-Romagna. Half medieval lanes and half green avenues and parks, Ferrara is home to one of Europe’s most imposing red-brick castles, one that provides a home to an annual journalism festival run by the magazine Internazionale. Ferrara is also known for a cake. In fact, it was after a discussion about translation and fact-checking with the Italian writer Do
title: Rachel Roddy’s recipe for torta tenerina, or rich chocolate cake | A kitchen in Rome

author: Martin Belam
description:
Test yourself on topical news trivia, pop culture and general knowledge every Thursday. How will you fare?

The recent US elections reminded the Thursday quiz that we have just passed the sixth anniversary of Rudy Giuliani’s Four Seasons Total Landscaping press conference, which was not only hilarious in and of itself, but sparked one of the best viral laughing videos of all internet history. Whether you will be laughing as hard after facing this week’s quiz remains to be seen. Here are 15 punchlines in search of a question about topical news, general knowledge and pop culture. Let’s be having you!

The Thursday news quiz, No 272
title: Thursday news quiz: Booker prize winners, GTA sinners and free dinners

author: Michael Savage, Rachael Healy and Maeve McClenaghan
description:
References raise questions over whether claims about bankable stars have been ignored by entertainment industry

The comedy sketch opens in a doctor’s office, with a trouserless David Walliams apparently being treated for a fictional sexually transmitted disease. The doctor tells him it is bad news and he needs to contact “everyone you’ve been intimate with over the last year”.

The camera closes in on the comedian’s shocked expression before he gasps: “Everyone?”

Continue reading...
title: Years of onscreen jokes suggest Walliams’ reputation was ‘in plain sight’ within industry, insider says

author: Ammar Kalia
description:
No one wants to slog away in the kitchen while everyone else gets festive. Thanks to these hacks and recipes from professionals, you won’t have to

When it comes to cooking during the festive season, time is tight, fridge space is at a premium and the last thing you want is to be trapped in the kitchen while your family and friends enjoy the fruits of your labour. Luckily, there are plenty of ways to get ahead. “It’s all in the preparation,” says Tom Childs, the head chef at Kerridge’s in London. “Get organised like a commercial kitchen and you’ll be relaxed by the time the big day arrives.”

From freezable, deeply delicious gravy to flavoured butters guaranteed to give the driest of meats a juicy kick, from preserves to liven up leftovers to lightweight puddings the whole family can enjoy, I tested the recipes chefs recommend making now to guarantee your Christmas larder is well stocked, no matter who ends up at y
title: ‘Christmas is all in the preparation!’ Chefs on eight easy things to do now – so you can relax on the big day

author: Kaya Genç
description:
Selahattin Demirtaş lit up the Turkish left in 2014, but was imprisoned for ‘terrorist propaganda’. His freedom would mark a new political era

A decade and a half ago, a promising figure emerged on Turkey’s political scene: Selahattin Demirtaş. A tall, talented, human rights lawyer then still in his 30s, a founder of Amnesty’s Diyarbakır branch in eastern Turkey, he was adept at thinking on his feet. And could he talk. His witty satirical speeches, broadcast on the evening news, annoyed Turkey’s establishment politicians on the right and left alike.

Demirtaş’s meteoric rise began in 2010, when he became the chair of Turkey’s main pro-Kurdish party, the Pea
title: Even Erdoğan backs the release of Turkey’s brightest opposition leader. So why is he still in jail? | Kaya Genç

author: Imogen West-Knights
description:
In 2022 and 2023, Hartshead Moor East, near Leeds, was voted the worst in Great Britain. Ever since, staff have been on a mission to redeem its reputation

  • The crime issue of the Long Read magazine is out now. Click here to order

In October 2023, at a service station on the M1 north-east of Leeds, Janine Gray received some bad news. She was surrounded by journalists and leading lights from the transport industry: people from the AA, the RAC, motorway service area chief executives, officials from National Highways. The big dogs. And it was among these gathered dignitaries that Gray heard the news she had been hoping, for the previous 12 months, not to hear. For the second year running, Hartshead Moor East – one half of the motorway services near Leed
title: ‘We can’t be at the bottom indefinitely’: Can Britain’s most maligned service station be turned around?

author: Stuart Heritage
description:
Substackers in love, dodgy romance scams and Jeff Bezos as the dashing lead … the film-makers behind the remake of the dial-up classic will be facing an embarrassment of pitches

Assuming you have already heard about the You’ve Got Mail reboot, you are probably in one of two states. You are either excited that the news might be a signal of a long overdue romcom resurgence, or you are embittered because it’s another sign that Hollywood has run out of original ideas.

I hold absolutely no truck with the latter view. Quite frankly, if there was ever a film in dire need of a reboot, then it’s You’ve Got Mail. The film is almost 28 years old, and it shows every single day of its age. You’ve seen it, you know how it goes. It’s about two people who use the futuristic new technology of email (email is no longer new) to communicate, despite being rival booksellers (
title: You had me at LOL: some notes for the You’ve Got Mail reboot

author: Arifa Akbar
description:
Skeleton suits for Phantom of the Opera, garish wigs for Beetlejuice, a Don’t Tell Mama dress for Cabaret … our critic meets the crowds going wild for costumes – and attends Cats in kitty costume

It’s an hour before curtain-up and the queue outside the theatre is full of green wigs and blue faces, all amid a sea of black and white stripes. It is Halloween night and these theatregoers of all ages, snaking around a corner of the West End, are in themed dress for the musical Beetlejuice, adapted from the 80s film.

In other theatres’ queues you might spot a king from Hamilton, the queens of Six and the wizards of Harry Potter and the Cursed Child, all bestowing new meaning to the idea of dressing up for the theatre.

Continue reading...
title: I wear a feline leotard and ears to see Cats – and meet all the other theatre superfans going crazy for costumes

author: Raphael Rashid in Seoul
description:
Seoul’s ‘scarf uncle’ has become a South Korean sensation for a sales technique that consists of talking customers out of purchases

By mid-morning the main alley of Namdaemun market in Seoul is ringed by private security guards and police, and the queue – penned behind a cordon – shuffles forward clutching numbered tickets. Those in it, mostly middle-aged women, have waited more than an hour.

In front of them, a stall holder is selling scarves, offering a deal of six for 10,000 won (about $6.80), roughly $1.15 each. The salesman – who is known by nicknames such as “scarf ajeossi”, or scarf uncle – has become something of a national sensation for a sales technique that consists of talking customers out of purchases. “Don’t spend your money,” he quips. “It doesn’t suit you.”

Continue reading...
title: ‘He’s the hottest thing right now’: how a $1 scarf seller became Seoul’s biggest attraction

author: Maya Yang
description:
SS United States, which set transatlantic speed record during maiden voyage in 1952, is sunk off coast of Destin

The historic SS United States has reached the end of its journey at sea, sinking Wednesday off the coast of Destin, Florida, where it will begin a new life underwater as an artificial reef.

The nearly 1,000ft American-made vessel, once the fastest ocean liner in the world, was launched in 1952 and made history by setting a transatlantic speed record during its maiden voyage. The ship carried thousands of passengers across the Atlantic over 17 years of operation before being retired in 1969.

Continue reading...
title: Historic US ocean liner sinks near Florida to become world’s largest artificial reef

author: Uwa Ede-Osifo in Los Angeles
description:
Animal that menaced residents was shot in October but then reappeared – and was shot for a second time and killed

A coyote that California wildlife officials believed they had euthanized after it bit a toddler and menaced residential pets in a trendy Los Angeles neighborhood was seen alive recently, neighborhood residents said.

Wiley, the name some Atwater Village residents gave to the coyote, had vexed the area with its increasingly aggressive and brazen behavior. The wild animal, which scampered through people’s backyards, was reportedly being fed by an unidentified man. Wiley’s presence drew local uproar after he bit a 16-month-old child.

Continue reading...
title: Coyote officials thought they had killed after child attack seen alive in LA neighborhood

author: Lorenzo Tondo
description:
Since the US war on Iran began in February, there have been hundreds of oil spills, posing a ‘generational’ threat to wildlife

The vast, dark slicks in the strait of Hormuz are visible from space. Throughout October, oil tankers were struck by missiles or sea mines in the waterway and spilled crude into the sea. The pollution has spread across the Gulf, contaminating coastlines and threatening to cause lasting damage to marine ecosystems that are home to dolphins, sea turtles and countless species of fish.

Eight months into the war between the US and Iran, one of the world’s busiest oil shipping routes has become a battlefield and the centre of a growing environmental disaster.

Contin
title: Oil slicks seen from space: the devastating impact of boat strikes on fragile Gulf ecosystems

author: Oliver Milman in Antalya, Turkey
description:
Failure to cut emissions will ‘consign humanity to disasters they are unable to adapt to’, report says

The world is heading for an “irrecoverable overshoot” of global temperature thresholds that will plunge billions of people into disastrous climate impacts because governments have stalled for so long to cut planet-heating emissions, analysis has found.

Under current policies, the planet will heat up by 2.7C on average by the end of the century compared with preindustrial times, the report by Climate Action Tracker (CAT) found. This is up slightly from a prediction of 2.6C in the group’s analysis conducted last year.

Continue reading...
title: World heading for ‘irrevocable overshoot’ of global temperature thresholds, analysis warns

description:

A teenage boy has been found alive after disappearing in dense bushland wearing only shorts and work boots nearly a week ago.

Police AirWing found William, 17, whose surname has not been shared, on Thursday morning.

title: Australian teen who went missing in bushland wearing only shorts and boots found alive after six days

description:
Huang’s potential departure would leave a leadership vacuum at the roughly $4tn chipmaker he co-founded, with Nvidia’s shares sliding about 8% in ​after-hours trading

Nvidia’s shares plunged in ⁠after-hours trading on news that its board may oust longtime CEO Jensen Huang, with the chipmaker losing about $600bn ‌in stock market value this week since the board announced its investigation into his relationship with a Chinese businesswoman.

Shares in Nvidia slid more than 8% after close of trade.
