author: Guardian staff and agencies
description:
Ukrainian president says he hopes Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner get ‘specifics’ from Moscow meeting after trilateral talks in Abu Dhabi. What we know on day 1,723

Volodymyr Zelenskyy said there could be a chance to reach a breakthrough this year in negotiations to end the war, as he arrived in Ireland ahead of talks with US envoys on Thursday. “Today there really is this opportunity, this window of opportunity, when all those participants who are now engaged in the negotiation process, genuinely want to achieve a result before 2027,” the Ukrainian president said. He is to meet the US presidential envoys, Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, after they return from a meeting with Russian president Vladimir Putin in Moscow. “What’s important is that the Americans flew to Putin with specifics,” Zelenskyy said. “I would very much like them to return to Dublin with specifics.”

The comments came after Russia and Ukraine agreed to the “largest prisoner ex
title: Ukraine war briefing: Zelenskyy sees ‘window of opportunity’ for peace as US envoys to meet Putin

author: Geoff Lemon
description:
Australia captain can confront ball tampering scandal with transparency about former team environment and how its members made their choices

In March 2018, Steve Smith was handed a shit sandwich by Cricket Australia. Smith had helped in its preparation, as captain of an Australia team whose ball tampering experiments on their tour of South Africa had got out of control, but it was always questionable that CA limited the blame to Smith, David Warner and Cameron Bancroft. Usman Khawaja’s recent revelations have added context that Smith adamantly took the fall to spare others. It is not in truth good leadership to perpetuate a lie, but Smith would reasonably have believed that his first job was to protect his men. Sometimes, you just have to tuck in.

Eight-and-a-half years later, current Test captain Pat Cummins has been handed a shit sandwich of his own. This one is in the form of Khawaja’s book, detailing the 2018 team’s
title: Pat Cummins can end sandpaper saga with full disclosure of what players knew – not what they didn’t | Geoff Lemon

author: Raphael Rashid and Natasha May
description:
For some, it’s their first big break, for others it’s a chance to secure their fame. But for all 11 acts, it’s an opportunity to be Asia’s first ever winner

  • Eurovision is heading to Asia: here’s what to expect

Next week the Eurovision juggernaut beloved by millions across Europe will arrive in Bangkok for its inaugural Asian edition, with organisers hoping for all the fanfare that the glitzy song contest usually brings.

Countries are getting behind their acts, particularly on social media, but much of the region is still familiarising itself with the competition; there are no big fanbases like those that have developed over the past seven decades in Europe.
title: The bar singer, the K-pop veteran and the ‘railway track diva’: meet three Eurovision Asia 2026 hopefuls

author: Associated Press
description:
Three-story building was at the edge of a construction site where another edifice had been demolished

Firefighters dug through the rubble of a three-story building in Brooklyn on Wednesday after it collapsed at the edge of a construction site, killing at least one person and trapping others beneath the wreckage.

Firefighters were called to the scene in the borough’s Flatbush section at about 4pm. News helicopter footage showed dozens of firefighters scouring the debris, with a group homing in on one area and appearing to use a saw to cut through the wreckage.

Continue reading...
title: Brooklyn building collapse kills at least one and traps others in wreckage

author: Severin Carrell Scotland editor
description:
Once thought to have been looted by Scottish tribes, the gilded limb is the centrepiece of a new exhibition on Roman Scotland in Edinburgh

A large bronze leg found in a bog in rural Scotland more than 200 years ago and then hidden away in a duke’s storeroom is helping to rewrite the history of the Roman empire.

Antiquarians argued that the so-called Mislington leg had been looted, perhaps from York, hacked off by marauding Scottish tribes and carried north over Hadrian’s Wall. “We cannot visualise the conditions which would have led to its erection anywhere north of the Great Wall,” said one scholar, James Curle, in 1932.

Continue reading...
title: Bronze leg found in Scottish bog sheds new light on Roman occupation
